name: pattern-hunter
label: Pattern hunter
description: Any eligible US stock, long or short. Aggressively trades sudden moves and recurring patterns from a morning screen of the most unusual moves, with news to tell overreactions from real information.

sessions.feedback: Digest labels the move as for 'the previous session 2026-11-25' with no flag that 11-26 was a holiday. The pre-market ADR gaps (Brazil +9-17%) are holiday catch-up and look like screen signals; flagging non-trading-day catch-up would help. Pre-market SPY/QQQ prints have proven unreliable predictors of the close (11-25 pre -1.9% -> -0.29%). Otherwise nothing blocked me.

Nothing blocked me this session. Two small requests. (1) The scan/digest pre-market column for thin prints is noisy, so a field showing the pre-market price along with the IEX last trade time would help. (2) For 'extend' orders it is unclear whether stop_pct/target_pct are measured from the last close or from a fill; I assumed the last close. A one-line note in the tool description would help.

No tool failures. Two suggestions. (1) The screen's pre-market column and the quotes tool sometimes disagree (BURL +7.8% vs a headline saying it tumbled) and the 1d % is not adjusted for special dividends (CHA -15.8% was an ex-dividend date). A flag for ex-dividend dates on the screen would stop wasted research on false 'down, no news' rows. (2) The digest's top-gainer list only shows one stock; a fuller top-loser list with news flags would help. Also it would help if get_quotes showed 'time since last trade' for stale IEX prints.

read_page failed on investing.com and aol.com URLs that came from web_search, so I fell back to the search-result content field. It would help if read_page could say why a fetch failed, or if the digest listed a few key market stories with text. A tool for the previous session's intraday path (e.g. the SPY open-to-close move) would help judge whether pre-market relief rallies fade. Nothing else held me back.

Nothing blocked me. Two small points. read_page failed on a gurufocus URL that the search had returned, so the helper cannot fetch every domain. A pre-open tool that shows pre-market moves with their news reason would save several calls. The screen's 'stories' count showed 0 for INSM and TU even though takeover or bid news existed, so treat that column as unreliable.

The screen's 'vs industry' column was misleading for TENB: the industry bucket 'Computer Software: Prepackaged' is broad, so a cybersecurity sector move looked like a stock-specific +15.6% outlier. A finer industry or peer-group field would help. The digest's 'stories' and news timestamps are often mislabeled (articles dated 11-19 describe 11-18 moves). In code_execution, helper functions and imports are lost between cells, which cost me two failed runs. It would help if the first-line summary of offering news included the offering price, because YSWY's pricing could not be found. Otherwise no blockers.

Nothing blocked me. Two things would have helped: (1) the screen's 1d % is not dividend-adjusted, which was the cause of the GAM/CET false signals earlier. An ex-dividend flag, or an adjusted return, would save research calls. (2) Price levels in the news (for example JD at about $105 in articles against $25 in the scan) and some company names look inconsistent with real-world data. I only used news for narrative and took prices from the tools.

The screen's 1d % is not dividend-adjusted, so closed-end funds going ex-dividend (GAM -12%, CET -6.6%) show up as top 'unusual moves'. Flagging ex-dividend dates, or adjusting for them, would save research budget. The earnings column also only says 'time not given', and consensus EPS or revenue figures would help with the surprise direction. Nothing blocked a trade this session.
Nothing blocking. A tool giving peer earnings dates and a post-earnings after-hours price would help.

The web_search result inside code_execution came back as a JSON string, so it had to be parsed with json.loads. Search results for specific recent news are poor and often years old. A direct news-by-ticker tool would help.
web_search in code_execution returns a JSON string rather than a list, which is not obvious from the docs. The digest has no pre-market prices for all names, but otherwise nothing held me back.

Examined and passed: NTNX (CEO exit, +2.6% pre), HPQ (+11.5% earnings chase), IMKTA (-11% NI -28%; 0.5% slippage), PHAR/Pharming (-24% Ruconest manufacturing pause, not shortable), VERA (+16% sympathy), CENT/CENTA (weak guide then no-news slide), Brazil ADR holiday catch-up gaps (no edge), AI rebound names (SNDK/IREN/MU; no short after 11-23 showed rebounds can run).
Next session (Mon 11-30): ARDT/TEVA/WCN vs stops (14.42 / 37.20 / 176.86); VRTX vs ~490 and whether it holds 510-520 (defensive rotation risk); CRTX MSCI index event 11-30; ANT vs 83 IPO floor; NTNX as CEO-exit test. NOTES (updated 2026-11-27)

PATTERN LOG
- 'news gap-down drift' (short large-cap earnings gap-downs, closed near lows, heavy vol): FIS short opened 11-05 @29.75; 25.83 low 11-20; bounced 3 days to 27.64 (pre 11-27 28.10, near stop 28.18) -> CLOSED 11-27 at ~+5.5% (check code record). Takeover tail risk on a 60%-off-high large cap (GPN/GTCR chatter).  UNM short closed 11-17 -5%.
- 'news gap-up drift': ECPG long 11-06 -> stopped -12.4% (-13.1 vs SPY). Peer PRAA -37% next day. Lesson: check peer earnings; buying day after gap-up is chasing.
- 'headline overreaction (non-earnings incident)': WCN long 11-18 7% (185-187 vs 179.89 entry, +4%, target 192.78, stop 176.86, horizon 12-07). TEVA long 11-20 3% (39.86 vs 38.50, +3.5%, stop 37.20, horizon 12-04). Both working so far in a market that fell; both are defensives and lag in rebounds (pre 11-27: WCN -1.2%, TEVA -1.8% vs SPY +1.7%). VRTX long opened 11-27 (see below).
- 'secondary offering overhang reversal': ARDT long 11-19 at 14.37-14.50 offering; 15.85 on 11-25 (+10%). Stop 14.42, target 16.99, horizon 12-03.
- 'regulatory delay overreaction' (new, 11-27): VRTX -7.5% pre (523 vs 564, 52w high 571 the day before) after FDA extended povetacicept PDUFA 11-30 -> by 2-28-27 (major amendment / info request). Analysts (JPM OW 570, Citi Buy 585, TD Cowen 575) say not thesis-changing; peak sales $3.4-4B so $10B mkt cap loss looks too big. Risk: info-driven drift, healthcare defensive rotation unwinding in a risk-on rebound, Vera (VERA +16%) takes first-mover share. Long 5%, stop -7%, target +7%, 10d. Judge by whether VRTX holds ~510-520.
- Screen history stats noisy: news-driven rows go on ~45-60%; no robust edge. 11-24 and 11-25 screens: no-news UP rows reversed (2 of 8 went on, -1.6% vs SPY); no-news DOWN rows continued (2/4 on 11-25, mixed). 11-23 opposite (up-no-news +3.8%). Don't over-trust.

DATA TRAPS
- Screen 1d % NOT dividend-adjusted (closed-end ex-div dates e.g. BGR -8% pre 11-27; CHA 11-23 special dividend). Always check special dividends on 'down, no news' rows.
- Pre-market prints on <1% of avg volume are noise. Scan pre-market % can be stale vs quotes. Holiday gaps in Brazil ADRs (ELPC/UGP/TIMB/VIV/AFYA +9-17% pre 11-27) are catch-up for the missed US session (B3 traded 11-26), not an edge.
- Pre-market SPY extremes have faded intraday as often as they extended (11-25 pre -1.9% -> close -0.29%; 11-23 pre +2.7% -> +4.7%).
- web_search from code: DEFINE helper functions in the SAME code cell as the call. `await web_search({"query":..})` inside async main(); result may be JSON string or list. Gurufocus 'down X% without company news' auto-articles list sector peers.
- read_page works on finexus/startupfortune-type articles; failed on investing.com and aol.com. Use search-result `content` first.
- Names in this universe can be fictional/odd (NVDA +31.5% one day, ANT = Anthropic IPO 83, SPCX $1.7T cap). Trust scan/get_quotes for levels.
- 'vs industry' column misleading when bucket is broad. 'stories: 0' does not mean no news; always run news(). Shortability changes day to day (ANT).

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock, long or short. You have one goal: exploit sudden price moves
and recurring market patterns aggressively and cleverly. How you do that is up to you.

Each morning you get a screen of the last session's most unusual moves among all eligible stocks:
each move in units of the stock's own volatility and net of its industry, volume against its
average, the gap, where it closed in its range, the run-up before, the 52-week range, pre-market
trading, news stories and earnings. The scan tool gives the same row for any ticker, so check peers,
suppliers and sympathy moves. Below the screen, code shows how each pattern you have named has done
and how earlier screen rows moved afterwards.

What published research says. Test it; your own record counts for more:
- Big moves with no identifiable news have tended to partly reverse over days to a few weeks. Moves
  backed by real information (earnings, guidance, analyst changes, deals) have tended to keep
  drifting, bad news especially. The reversal is cleaner measured against the industry and in stocks
  whose volume did not explode; heavy volume has tended to mean continuation.
- Stocks bought heavily by retail traders on attention spikes have tended to fall back over the
  following weeks.
- You fill at the open. Overnight moves have tended to carry on through the open and fade during the
  day, so buying a hyped gap-up at the open is a poor entry, and a pre-market that has already undone
  the move leaves little to take.
- Reversal trades pay for providing liquidity, and pay best when markets are stressed. They fail when
  the move had news, when the whole industry moved, and in sharp rebounds after a sell-off, when
  shorting the losers hurts most. Crowded shorts can squeeze.
- Many patterns weakened after they were published, and smaller stocks cost more to trade here: a
  round trip is about 0.2% in large caps and 1% in the smallest.

How to work:
- Start from the screen. Take the rows that look most mispriced, find out why each moved (read the
  news, check the earnings date and the pre-market), and decide what is left to take at the open.
- Be aggressive when the evidence lines up: size up, short spikes you can explain, run several
  positions on a busy day. Doing nothing because you did not look is the failure this agent exists to
  avoid. When you pass, say in your summary which rows you examined and why each was not a trade.
- Every trade names its pattern, says why the price is wrong and what would prove you wrong, and has
  an exit. Reuse a pattern's name whenever you trade the same idea, so its record builds up.
- Set stops for the pattern: a reversal needs room to work, so a stop inside the stock's normal daily
  range mostly sells the bounce. Size by how volatile the stock is.
- Keep a pattern log in your notes: what each pattern is, the trades behind it, how they did against
  SPY, and whether you still believe it. Trust the code-written records over your memory. Drop what
  keeps losing and try new patterns you spot.
